acceptedAnswer.text: A physician-owned hospital (POH) is a hospital where physicians hold an ownership stake. These facilities are typically smaller, more specialized, and have been shown to deliver higher patient satisfaction and better outcomes in many specialties. Federal law (the Stark Law/ACA Section 6001) has restricted the growth of new physician-owned hospitals since 2010, though existing facilities can continue to operate.

mainEntity.name: What is a Certificate of Need (CON) law?

acceptedAnswer.text: Certificate of Need (CON) laws are state regulations that require healthcare providers to obtain government approval before building new facilities, expanding services, or purchasing major equipment. Currently, 35 states and Washington D.C. have some form of CON law. Critics argue CON laws protect incumbent hospital monopolies and reduce competition, while supporters claim they prevent unnecessary duplication of services.
